citability_verdict: Four source types are safe to put on a public page, in this order of strength. (1) Statutory filings — SEC EDGAR (Ciena's 8-K Exhibit 99.1, Fabrinet's 10-K, Coherent's 10-K), SZSE/cninfo (Innolight, Eoptolink, Accelink, 天孚通信) and JPX (Fujikura) — are free, permanent and director-attested; always prefer the exchange-hosted copy over a company website mirror (Accelink re-uploaded its own PDF four days after the statutory disclosure) or a data-vendor mirror (东方财富's Eoptolink copy is byte-identical but mirrors rot), and prefer the filing over any third party's currency conversion of it. (2) Research houses' own free press releases and newsletters — LightCounting LightTrends, Cignal AI press releases, TrendForce press center, Dell'Oro news — are citable with attribution even though the underlying reports cost ~$6,000, because the headline number sits outside the gate; the discipline is to attribute to the specific issue ("LightCounting, Q2 Quarterly Market Update, June 2026"), not to a bare house name or year, because every one of these houses revises its own numbers within months and the superseded figure usually ranks higher in search. Note that WebFetch-style agents get HTTP 403 from lightcounting.com and stale CDN copies from cignal.ai and trendforce.com: that is bot filtering and edge caching, not a paywall, and a summarizer "confirming" a quote on such a fetch is worthless — verify from raw HTML or a real browser. (3) A paywalled research number becomes publishable when a listed issuer reproduces it in a mandatory filing, as Accelink does with Omdia — but it must be worded "per Omdia data as cited in Accelink's FY2025 annual report", never "Omdia says", since the underlying tracker cannot be independently checked and the issuer is an interested party. (4) Chinese trade press (C114) is safe only as the readable carrier of detail the primary source does not print in text — here ranks 6/7/8/10 — with the ranking itself attributed to LightCounting; C114 URLs are unstable (the originally submitted one 404s), so pin the article ID and keep the mobile mirror. Never publish: anything from a paid report body; numbers whose only home is a search-engine snippet (the "InnoLight 23.4%" share line appears nowhere on LightCounting's page and contradicts Eoptolink ranking #2); a figure read off an image without archiving the image (LightCounting's Top-10 PNG is overwritten annually and last year's already 404s); or any share computed by dividing one house's numerator into another house's denominator, since transceivers, transceivers-plus-AOCs, datacom optical components, all optical components and optical transport systems are five different bases in this payload.
